previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted due to hyperglycemia and mechanical falls in the setting of multiple myeloma and chemotherapy. He presented with blood glucose levels in the 500s, poor oral intake, and worsening peripheral neuropathy leading to multiple falls. His long-acting insulin had been discontinued months prior, contributing to poor glycemic control. He received a platelet transfusion for thrombocytopenia and was restarted on glargine insulin with improved glucose levels. A CT head and chest X-ray showed no acute abnormalities. MRI of the spine revealed a stable T12 compression fracture and degenerative changes without cord compression. He received Velcade chemotherapy during admission. His anticoagulation was held due to low platelets and to be resumed outpatient. He was discharged home with a rolling walker, home health services, and follow-up appointments with his oncologist, endocrinologist, and primary care provider.

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient presented to the Emergency Department on ___. Pt 
was evaluated by anaesthesia/ Upon arrival to ED imaging 
revealed fractures of left ribs ___.  No other injuries were

Neuro: After becoming sober the patient had brief episodes of 
confusion which were treated with benzodiazepines, and resolved. 
 At the time of discharge he was calm, conscious, alert, and 
oriented. Pain was initially managed with a morphine PCA and 
then transitioned to oral oxycodone once tolerating a diet.
 
CV: The patient remained stable from a cardiovascular 
standpoint; vital signs were routinely monitored.  Asymptomatic 
hypertension was noted and treated with IV beta blockers and 
hydralazine, and became stable on the patient's home 
medications.

Pulmonary: The patient remained stable from a pulmonary 
standpoint; vital signs were routinely monitored. Good pulmonary 
toilet, early ambulation and incentive spirometry were 
encouraged throughout hospitalization, although ambulation was 
limited by thoracic cage pain initially. 

GI/GU/FEN: The patient was initially kept NPO. On HD#2 the 
patient was confused and complained of abdominal discomfort with 
vomiting.  KUB revealed a distended stomach, and an NG tube was 
placed.  On HD#3, the NGT was removed without complications, 
which was tolerated well, therefore, the diet was advanced 
sequentially to a Regular diet, which was well tolerated. 
Patient's intake and output were closely monitored

ID: The patient's fever curves were closely watched for signs of 
infection, of which there were none.

HEME: The patient's blood counts were closely watched for signs 
of bleeding, of which there were none.  His blood counts 
remained stable at his baseline, with his platelet count lower 
than previous.  Given this, his warfarin was held at the 
recommendation of his hematology/oncology team, which will be 
re-evaluated at his next appointment.

Prophylaxis: ___ dyne boots were used during this stay and was 
encouraged to get up and ambulate as early as possible.

At the time of discharge, the patient was doing well, afebrile 
and hemodynamically stable.  The patient was tolerating a diet, 
ambulating, voiding without assistance, and pain was well 
controlled.  The patient received discharge teaching and 
follow-up instructions with understanding verbalized and 
agreement with the discharge plan.

the pain medication is too sedating take half the dose and 
notify your physician.
 
* Pneumonia is a complication of rib fractures.  In order to 
decrease your risk you must use your incentive spirometer 4 
times every hour while awake.  This will help expand the small 
airways in your lungs and assist in coughing up secretions that 
pool in the lungs.

against your chest and guard your rib cage while coughing and 
deep breathing.

periods may ease the pain.

should take a stool softener twice daily and increase your fluid 
and fiber intake if possible.

effects so make sure your doctor approves.

shortness of breath, increased pain or crackling sensation 
around your ribs (crepitus).

TECHNIQUE:  Routine unenhanced head CT was performed and viewed in brain,
intermediate and bone windows.  Coronal and sagittal reformats were also
performed.

DOSE:  DLP: 1895 mGy-cm; CTDI:  159 mGy

COMPARISON:  CT head ___

FINDINGS: 

There is no acute intracranial hemorrhage, edema, mass effect or large
territorial infarction. Again there is an old left putamen infarct. Minimal
periventricular white matter hypodensities are nonspecific but may reflect
sequela of chronic microvascular ischemic disease. Mild prominence of the
ventricles and sulci is unchanged indicating age-related atrophy. There is no
hydrocephalus.

There is no fracture.

Right mastoid is underpneumatized but clear. Right middle ear cavities clear.
Left mastoid has no pneumatized air cells. Left mastoid antrum is opacified,
and left middle ear cavity is partially opacified. These findings are
unchanged. Visualized paranasal sinuses are well aerated.

IMPRESSION:


1. No evidence for acute intracranial abnormalities.
2. Chronic left mastoid and middle ear abnormalities, as detailed above.

Multiplanar axial, coronal sagittal images were generated.

COMPARISON:  CT chest ___. CT abdomen and pelvis ___.

FINDINGS: 

CT CHEST WITH CONTRAST: The partially visualized thyroid is normal. There is
no lymphadenopathy. The esophagus is grossly normal. The heart is not enlarged
and there is no pericardial effusion. Aorta and main thoracic vessels are well
opacified and normal in caliber. The main pulmonary arteries are normal in
caliber. There is no mediastinal hematoma.

There may be a tiny left apical pneumothorax (03:39). There are mild dependent
changes but no worrisome focal nodule or opacity. There is no pleural
effusion.

CT ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST: The liver is diffusely hypoattenuating without focal
lesions or biliary duct dilation. The gallbladder, spleen, pancreas, adrenal
glands and kidneys are normal. The ureters are normal throughout their
visualized course.

The stomach, small marked bowel are normal in caliber without wall thickening
or obstruction. There is no free air.  There is no mesenteric retroperitoneal
lymphadenopathy.

CT PELVIS WITH CONTRAST: The prostate is surgically absent. The urinary
bladder is collapsed around a Foley catheter. There is a small fat containing
right inguinal hernia. There is a trace amount of nonhemorrhagic fluid in the
pelvis.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES: There is a minimally displaced right first rib fracture.
There are multiple left-sided rib fractures including the third, fourth,
fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth and nineth. There are chronic deformities of the
superior pubic rami bilaterally.

IMPRESSION:


1. Right first rib fracture and numerous left rib fractures as detailed above.
2. Possible tiny left apical pneumothorax.
3. Fatty liver.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with ? small bowel injury after MVC.  increasing

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial images were acquired through abdomen and pelvis
following intravenous contrast administration with split bolus technique.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and submitted to PACS for
review.
Oral contrast was administered.

DOSE:  DLP: 930.90 mGy-cm (abdomen and pelvis.
IV Contrast:  130 mL Omnipaque.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis ___.

FINDINGS: 

A small left pleural effusion is present with bibasilar atelectasis. The
visualized heart and pericardium are unremarkable.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY:  The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesions.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic
or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder is within normal limits,
without stones or gallbladder wall thickening.
PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.
SPLEEN:  The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.
ADRENALS:  The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.
URINARY: The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is no evidence of stones, focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis. There
are no urothelial lesions in the kidneys or ureters. There is no perinephric
abnormality.
GASTROINTESTINAL:  An enteric tube is noted, terminating in the stomach. 
Small bowel loops demonstrate normal caliber, wall thickness and enhancement
throughout.  Oral contrast reaches the there proximal jejunum. Colon and
rectum are within normal limits. There is no evidence of small or large bowel
injury. Specifically, there is no free fluid, free air, or extraluminal oral
contrast within the abdomen or pelvis.  There is no abnormality in the
mesentery concerning for injury.
RETROPERITONEUM:  There is no evidence of retroperitoneal and mesenteric
lymphadenopathy.
VASCULAR:  There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  There is no calcium burden
in the abdominal aorta and great abdominal arteries.

PELVIS:

A Foley is present in a collapsed bladder. Surgical clips in the prostate bed
and iliac lymph node chains bilaterally are noted. There is no evidence of
pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.  There is no free fluid in the pelvis.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES:

A stable lytic lesion along the anterior superior endplate of T12 with mild
anterior wedging is noted.  Heterotopic new bone formation near the symphysis
pubis may be due to prior trauma. Nondisplaced rib fractures of left posterior
ribs 8 and 9 are noted.Abdominal and pelvic wall is within normal limits.

IMPRESSION: 

1. No direct or indirect evidence of bowel or mesenteric injury.
2.  Small left pleural effusion with bibasilar atelectasis.
3.  Stable lytic lesion in the T12 vertebral body.
